scenario: 60 分钟远程 AI 编码面试：面试官只能看你的屏幕、听你的话，你大半时间在跟 AI 打字对话。
scenario_en: It's a 60-minute remote AI coding interview: the interviewer only sees your screen and hears you, and most of your typing goes into the AI chat.
q: AI 编码面试里的沟通为什么比传统面试更难？
q_en: Why is communication in an AI coding interview harder than in a traditional interview?
options: 因为必须提前背熟一套提示词模板才能用
因为面试官全程看不到你共享的屏幕内容
因为你同时要对 AI 和对面试官两条线沟通
因为 AI 输出的代码内容按规定不能被讨论
why: 决定性因素是你要同时维持两条沟通线——AI 和面试官；只顾 AI 会让面试官读不到你的判断过程。
why_en: AI coding interviews are harder to communicate through because you must run two conversations at once, with the AI and with the interviewer.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Candidate[Candidate] --> Interviewer[Interviewer]
  Candidate --> AI[AI tool]
  AI --> Candidate
  Candidate --> Code[Codebase]
  Code --> Interviewer
options_en: Because you have to memorize a prompt template in advance.
Because the interviewer can't see your shared screen at all.
Because you have to communicate on two channels at once, to the AI and to the interviewer.
Because the AI's code output is off-limits for discussion by policy.
optionExplanations: 背模板提示词不是沟通技巧，遇到没背过的场景照样卡壳，这不是难度的根源。
面试官其实能看到你的操作和输出，看不到的是你脑子里的判断过程。
对，两条线要同时兼顾——跟 AI 说清需求，也要让面试官跟上你的思路。
讨论 AI 输出恰恰是加分项，不是禁区，这个假设反了。
optionExplanations_en: Reciting fixed prompts isn't a skill — it breaks the moment the scenario isn't the one you memorized.
The interviewer can actually see your actions and output; what's hidden is your reasoning.
Right — you have to run both lines at once: tell the AI what you need and keep the interviewer with you.
Discussing AI output is a plus signal, not off-limits — this premise is backwards.

scenario: 你准备让 AI 给 Order 类实现输入校验。
scenario_en: You are about to ask the AI to add input validation to the Order class.
q: 提示 AI 前，最应该先对面试官说什么？
q_en: Before prompting the AI, what should you say to the interviewer first?
options: “我要给 Order 加校验，先查空字段和数量范围。”
“我先让 AI 随便试着写写看，再根据它写出来的结果调整方向。”
“等它写完了，我再跟你解释我当时是怎么推理的。”
“什么都不说，直接打字把校验的提示发给 AI。”
why: 决定性约束是面试官只能看到提示和输出、看不到你的思路；先说意图能把后续内容放进上下文。
why_en: State your intent before prompting so the interviewer can follow your plan instead of just watching you type.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是改一个显而易见的一行 typo，可以边改边说一句，不需要完整铺陈。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Intent[State intent] --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
  Prompt --> Review[Review output]
  Review --> Explain[Explain next step]
options_en: I'm going to add validation to Order, checking null fields and quantity range first.
I'll just let the AI take a random first pass, then decide my direction from whatever it gives me.
I'll wait until it's done, then explain how I was reasoning at the time.
I won't say anything, I'll just type the validation prompt straight to the AI.
tradeoff: 提示前先说明意图 vs 直接开始打字
optionExplanations: 先把校验范围说清楚，面试官立刻就能跟着你接下来的每一步走。
把决定权交给 AI 随便试，面试官只能等结果出来才知道你在做什么。
等写完再解释，等于面试官全程只看操作，事后补的上下文来得太晚。
什么都不说直接打字，面试官从头到尾看不到你的判断依据。
optionExplanations_en: Naming the validation scope up front lets the interviewer follow every step that comes after.
Handing it to a random first AI attempt means the interviewer only learns what you're doing once results appear.
Explaining after it's written means the interviewer watched blind the whole time — the context comes too late.
Typing straight into the prompt with no framing leaves your reasoning invisible from start to finish.

q: 把推荐的 AI 编码沟通节奏排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the recommended AI coding communication rhythm in the correct order:
steps: 审阅 AI 输出并说出是否符合预期
继续下一步或重新提示
说明你接下来要做什么
向 AI 发出具体提示
why: 有效节奏是先声明意图，再提示 AI，然后公开审阅结果，最后决定继续或修正。
why_en: The useful rhythm is state intent, prompt the AI, review aloud, then continue or correct course.
tradeoff: 先声明意图再行动 vs 先动手后解释
diagram:
flowchart LR
  SayPlan[Say plan] --> AskAI[Ask AI]
  AskAI --> Narrate[Narrate wait]
  Narrate --> Review[Review output]
  Review --> Next[State next move]

scenario: AI 一次吐出 60 行订单校验代码，你要在 40 分钟内交付并对最终代码的正确性负责。
scenario_en: The AI just dumped 60 lines of order-validation code, and you have 40 minutes and you own whether the final code is correct.
q: AI 生成代码后，哪些口头反馈是好信号？（多选）
q_en: After the AI generates code, which spoken reactions are good signals? (Select all that apply.)
options: “AI 写了，所以肯定对。”
“这符合我的目标，它检查了 null 字段和数量。”
“它用了异常，但项目里用 error object，我会重新提示。”
“这段很多，我先读一遍确认。”
why: 这些反馈展示你在验证、纠偏和主动审查；盲目接受 AI 输出是负面信号。
why_en: Good narration shows that you verify, correct, and review AI output rather than accepting it blindly.
options_en: The AI wrote it, so it must be correct.
This matches my goal, it checks for null fields and validates quantity.
It used exceptions, but this codebase uses error objects, so I'll reprompt.
This is a lot of code, let me read through it first to confirm.
optionExplanations: 把正确与否全部归给 AI，等于放弃了你自己的核验责任。
点名具体检查项，说明你真的核对了校验逻辑，不是走个过场。
抓到风格冲突还主动要求重提示，挡住了代码库风格不一致的隐患。
承认代码多要先读完，防止在没看懂全部改动前就草率通过。
optionExplanations_en: Crediting correctness to the AI alone means you've skipped your own verification duty.
Naming a specific check proves you actually verified the logic, not just went through the motions.
Catching the style mismatch and asking to reprompt blocks a codebase-style inconsistency before it lands.
Admitting you need to read it first stops you rubber-stamping changes you haven't actually reviewed.

scenario: 45 分钟 AI 编码面试，评分表打的是你的过程判断分，不是最终代码行数。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute AI coding interview, the rubric scores your judgment during the process, not the lines of code you end up with.
q: AI 编码面试里，面试官更应该被当成什么角色？
q_en: In an AI coding interview, what role should you treat the interviewer as?
options: 只看最终结果、不参与过程的考官
不能被打扰的旁观者
可以被 AI 取代的角色
和你一起结对写代码的伙伴
why: AI 编码面试更像结对编程，面试官需要持续听到你的意图、判断和修正才能评估你。
why_en: Treat the interviewer like a pair partner who needs to keep hearing your intent, judgment, and corrections.
options_en: An examiner who only looks at the final result and ignores the process.
A bystander you should not interrupt.
A role the AI can substitute for.
A pair-programming partner working alongside you.
tradeoff: 把面试官当结对伙伴持续沟通 vs 当考官只交最终结果
optionExplanations: 把面试官当只看结果的考官，会让你倾向沉默写代码，到最后才亮出成果。
把面试官当不能打扰的旁观者，你会不敢开口说思路，错过整个评估窗口。
跟 AI 讲清楚不等于跟面试官沟通，面试官听到的是你和 AI 的对话，不是你的判断。
对，把面试官当结对搭档，持续讲意图、判断和修正，让评估全程可见。
optionExplanations_en: Treating the interviewer as a results-only examiner tends to make you code silently until the very end.
Treating the interviewer as a bystander you shouldn't interrupt makes you afraid to voice your thinking at all.
Talking to the AI isn't the same as talking to the interviewer — they only hear your AI chat, not your judgment.
Right — treat the interviewer as a pair partner, narrating intent, judgment, and fixes the whole way.

q: 补全 AI 编码面试的推荐沟通节奏：
q_en: Complete the recommended communication rhythm for an AI coding interview:
text: 有效沟通节奏是：先说明{{意图}}，再提示 AI，接着公开{{审阅输出}}，最后说明{{下一步}}。
why: 这个节奏让面试官持续看到你在做决策，而不是把判断外包给 AI。
why_en: This rhythm keeps the interviewer aware that you are making the decisions, not outsourcing judgment to the AI.

scenario: AI 在结构化平台里响应很慢，屏幕上出现加载动画，你在等待生成结果。
scenario_en: The AI is slow to respond in a structured platform, and you are waiting on a loading spinner.
q: AI 还在生成时，这段等待时间最好怎么用？
q_en: While the AI is still generating, how should you best use the waiting time?
options: 一直沉默盯着加载动画，一句话也不解释
打开无关网页刷点别的东西，放松等结果出来
跟面试官讲你的方案、预期输出或边界条件
反复重复提交同一个提示，指望换个结果蹦出来
why: 等待时间正好用来填补空白——讲方案、预期输出或边界条件，正是面试官想听的判断和取舍。
why_en: Use AI wait time to talk through your approach, expected output, and edge cases instead of sitting in silence.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经说清方案，也可以利用等待时间阅读下一步代码或写测试草案。
options_en: Sit in total silence staring at the loading spinner, never explaining anything.
Open an unrelated webpage and scroll something else while you wait for it to finish.
Talk the interviewer through your approach, expected output, or edge cases.
Keep resubmitting the exact same prompt over and over, hoping a different result pops out.
tradeoff: 用等待时间讲思路 vs 沉默等结果
optionExplanations: 干等着不说话，等于让面试官白白错过了本来可以讲清楚的判断窗口。
刷点无关内容看着轻松，其实会被面试官解读为你已经脱离了这道题。
对，等待正好用来讲方案、预期输出或边界条件，这正是面试官想听的。
反复点提交对生成速度毫无帮助，纯粹在浪费本可以讲思路的时间。
optionExplanations_en: Waiting in silence just burns a window where you could've been walking the interviewer through your thinking.
Browsing something unrelated reads as checking out of the interview, even if it feels harmless.
Right — use the wait to talk through your approach, expected output, or edge cases, exactly what they want to hear.
Resubmitting the same prompt over and over does nothing for generation speed, it just burns narration time.

scenario: AI 每次生成要等 20-30 秒，一场 60 分钟面试里这类等待累计接近 10 分钟。
scenario_en: Each AI generation takes 20 to 30 seconds, so across a 60-minute interview that waiting adds up to nearly 10 minutes.
q: AI 生成期间可以并行做哪些有价值的事？（多选）
q_en: What useful work can you do in parallel while the AI is generating? (Select all that apply.)
options: 阅读下一阶段可能需要的代码
草拟当前步骤的测试用例
完全停下等 AI
思考边界条件
why: 并行阅读、写测试草案和想边界情况能让你更快，也让面试官看到你没有被动等待。
why_en: Reading ahead, drafting tests, and thinking through edge cases turn AI wait time into productive interview time.
options_en: Read the code you'll likely need for the next stage.
Sketch out test cases for the current step.
Stop completely and just wait for the AI.
Think through edge cases.
optionExplanations: 提前把下一步要用的代码摸清楚，减少提示下一步时现翻代码的等待。
先把测试草案写好，输出一出来就能立刻验证，不用现想测试点。
完全停下干等，错过了本可以并行处理的效率窗口，也显得被动。
提前想清楚边界情况，减少输出后因为漏想而返工的概率。
optionExplanations_en: Reading ahead the code you'll likely need cuts the dead time you'd spend digging through it later.
Drafting test cases early means you can verify the moment output lands, instead of thinking tests up cold.
Stopping completely wastes a window you could've used productively, and reads as passive.
Working through edge cases in advance cuts the rework that comes from missing them after the fact.

scenario: 远程面试中一次 AI 生成要 30 秒，这期间面试官屏幕上只有一个加载动画。
scenario_en: In a remote interview a single generation takes 30 seconds, and all the interviewer sees on screen is a spinner.
q: 长时间盯着 AI 加载动画不说话，最大的问题是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest problem with staring at the AI loading spinner in silence for a long time?
options: 面试官分不清你是在想、卡住还是干等
AI 会因此生成更差质量的代码结果
测试会因为你保持沉默而自动判定失败
代码库会因此丢失掉之前累积的上下文
why: 沉默本身不一定错，但不解释会让面试官失去你的思维轨迹，沟通成本立刻上升。
why_en: Unframed silence leaves the interviewer unable to tell whether you are thinking, stuck, or just waiting.
options_en: The interviewer can't tell if you're thinking, stuck, or just waiting passively.
The AI will generate lower-quality code as a result.
Tests will automatically fail because you stayed silent.
The codebase will lose the context it had built up.
optionExplanations: 对，安静的时候面试官只能靠猜——是在推演、卡住了还是纯粹发呆。
AI 生成质量只看提示和上下文，跟你说不说话没有任何因果关系。
测试通不通过只取决于代码逻辑，跟你保持沉默没有半点关系。
代码库的上下文是技术层面的状态，不会因为你没开口就凭空丢失。
optionExplanations_en: Right — silence alone gives the interviewer nothing to go on: thinking, stuck, or just idle, they can't tell.
Generation quality depends on the prompt and context, not on whether you're narrating out loud.
Test results depend purely on the code's logic, staying quiet has no bearing on that.
Codebase context is a technical state, it doesn't vanish just because you didn't speak.

scenario: 你在处理图问题时卡在如何检测和处理 cycle（环），已经原地绕了一会儿。
scenario_en: You are working on a graph problem and have been stuck for a while on detecting and handling cycles.
q: 发现自己卡住时，最好的沟通方式是什么？
q_en: When you realize you are stuck, what is the best way to communicate?
options: 继续保持沉默，独自消耗时间硬扛
让 AI 随机重写整个已有方案
假装问题已经解决，直接跳过这一步
说清楚卡在哪里，并向面试官请求建议
why: 请求帮助是协作而非失败；面试官更愿意看到你暴露阻塞点并继续推进，而不是沉默硬扛。
why_en: Naming a specific blocker and asking for help is collaboration and keeps the interview moving forward.
whenOtherWins: 如果你刚形成清晰假设，可以先用一分钟验证；超过这个时间就该显式沟通。
options_en: Stay silent and grind through it alone, burning time.
Have the AI randomly rewrite the whole existing solution.
Pretend the problem is already solved and skip straight past it.
Name exactly where you're stuck and ask the interviewer for suggestions.
tradeoff: 主动说出卡点求助 vs 独自沉默消耗时间

termDefinitions.meaning: 图论中指从一个节点出发、沿边走一圈能回到自己的路径，即环路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cycle is a path in a graph that starts and ends at the same node, forming a loop.

optionExplanations: 硬扛着不说话，只是把卡住的状态藏起来，时间照样在流失。
让 AI 随机重写整个方案，容易把已经验证过的部分也一起推倒。
假装解决了跳过去，一被追问细节就露馅，可信度反而受损。
对，把卡点说具体、主动请面试官给建议，是协作信号不是能力不足。
optionExplanations_en: Grinding through in silence just hides the blocker, the clock keeps running regardless.
A random full rewrite risks throwing out parts of the approach you'd already validated.
Faking a solution collapses the moment you get a follow-up question, and trust takes the hit.
Right — naming exactly where you're stuck and asking for input is collaboration, not weakness.

q: 补全转向（换方案）时应该说出的信息：
q_en: Complete what you should say when pivoting to a different approach:
text: 改变方向时要说明旧方案为什么{{不成立}}，新方案解决了什么{{约束}}，以及下一步怎么{{执行}}。
why: 解释转向能把看似混乱的重写变成可评估的适应能力。
why_en: Explaining a pivot turns a rewrite into evidence of adaptive problem solving.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Stuck[Stuck] --> Name[Name issue]
  Name --> Pivot[State pivot]
  Pivot --> NewPlan[New plan]
  NewPlan --> Continue[Continue]

scenario: 你发现当前暴力方案在大输入下会超时，准备换成堆优化（heap-based）方案。
scenario_en: You realize the current brute-force approach will time out on large inputs, so you are switching to a heap-based approach.
q: 换方案时，最好的口头说明是哪一句？
q_en: When changing approaches, which spoken explanation is best?
options: “暴力方案大输入会超时，我改用 heap 方案。”
“我全部删掉，从头把代码重新写一遍试试。”
“AI 说这里该换个方案，我就照着换了。”
“这里的实现应该差不多凑合着能用了，先不细看了。”
why: 好的转向说明要同时点名问题、原因和新计划，让面试官看到你是主动判断而非被动乱改。
why_en: A strong pivot statement names the flaw, the reason it matters, and the replacement approach.
whenOtherWins: 如果当前方案只是小 bug 而非复杂度根因，修补原方案会比整体换方向更稳。
options_en: The brute-force approach times out on large inputs, so I'm switching to a heap-based solution.
I'll delete it all and try rewriting the whole thing from scratch.
The AI said to switch to a different approach here, so I just went along with it.
This implementation should probably work well enough as it is, no need to look closer.
tradeoff: 点名问题+原因+新方案 vs 只说要换不说为什么

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种能快速取出最小值或最大值的树形数据结构，常用于优先队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heap is a tree-based data structure that gives fast access to the minimum or maximum element, often used as a priority queue.

optionExplanations: 对，点名问题、原因、替代方案三件一起说清楚，是可评估的转向。
只讲要重写、不说原因，面试官看到动作却猜不出背后的判断。
把判断权交给 AI 的建议，面试官学不到你自己的复杂度分析。
含糊说“差不多能用”，几乎不提供任何可评估的判断信息。
optionExplanations_en: Right — naming the flaw, the reason, and the replacement together is a pivot the interviewer can evaluate.
Announcing a rewrite without the reason leaves the interviewer watching the action, not the judgment behind it.
Deferring to what the AI suggested tells the interviewer nothing about your own complexity analysis.
'Should work well enough' is too vague to give the interviewer anything to evaluate.

scenario: 60 分钟面试进行到第 30 分钟，你发现选的数据结构撑不住需求，必须换方案。
scenario_en: You're 30 minutes into a 60-minute interview and you realize the data structure you picked can't carry the requirements, so you have to switch.
q: 走错方向后能清楚说明并转向，面试官通常如何评价？
q_en: How do interviewers usually view clearly explaining and pivoting after taking a wrong direction?
options: 一定比从头到尾都不犯错更差
说明候选人没办法独立使用 AI 完成任务
如果能识别问题并解释转向，反而是强信号
说明前面做的所有工作都直接作废
why: 很多死路难以提前看见，关键在于能否快速发现、说明原因并恢复推进。
why_en: Recognizing a dead end and pivoting cleanly is a stronger signal than silently tuning a flawed approach.
options_en: It's always worse than never making a mistake at all, start to finish.
It means the candidate can't use the AI independently to finish the task.
Recognizing the issue and explaining the pivot is actually a strong signal.
It means every bit of work done before that point is wasted.
optionExplanations: 把犯错本身当成绝对减分项，忽略了面试官真正在看的是恢复速度。
走错方向和会不会用 AI 是两件不相关的事，这个因果关系是错的。
对，能识别问题、讲清楚为什么转向，恰恰证明了判断力和适应力。
前面探索过的路径本身也在积累信息，并不是白费功夫。
optionExplanations_en: Treating any mistake as an automatic deduction ignores that interviewers really watch recovery speed.
Taking a wrong turn and AI proficiency are unrelated — this causal link doesn't hold.
Right — recognizing the problem and explaining the pivot is exactly what proves judgment and adaptability.
The path you already explored still built understanding, it wasn't wasted effort.

scenario: 60 分钟内要用 AI 写完三个功能，同时评分表要求你的推理过程全程可见。
scenario_en: You have 60 minutes to ship three features with the AI, and the rubric also requires your reasoning to stay visible throughout.
q: 编码时，兼顾速度与清晰度的最佳叙述粒度是什么？
q_en: While coding, what narration level best balances speed and clarity?
options: 逐字描述你敲下的每一个按键
只在决策、意外和修正这些拐点说明
完全不做任何解释，只保证写得快
每写完一行代码就完整读一遍
why: 高频细节拖慢节奏，完全沉默又失去评估窗口；只在拐点叙述能兼顾两者。
why_en: Narrating only decisions, surprises, and corrections balances speed with visible reasoning.
options_en: Narrate every single keystroke you type.
Narrate only at inflection points: decisions, surprises, and corrections.
Explain absolutely nothing and just optimize for typing speed.
Read every finished line of code out loud as you write it.
tradeoff: 只讲拐点 vs 逐字播报
optionExplanations: 逐个按键都播报，信息全被键盘噪音淹没，面试官根本抓不到重点。
对，只在决策、意外、修正这些拐点开口，既不拖节奏又保住评估窗口。
全程不解释确实快，但面试官从此失去了能跟上你判断的窗口。
每行都读一遍，大部分代码根本没有决策价值，纯粹拖慢速度。
optionExplanations_en: Narrating every keystroke drowns the signal in keyboard noise, the interviewer can't find the point.
Right — narrate only at inflection points: decisions, surprises, corrections. That keeps pace without going dark.
Staying fast by explaining nothing costs you the window the interviewer needs to follow your judgment.
Reading every line aloud slows you down for lines that carry no decision value at all.

scenario: 你在稳定推进代码，没有卡住，也没有需要特别强调的决策。
scenario_en: You are making steady coding progress, with no blocker and no major decision to call out.
q: 活跃编码时，怎样的进度叙述频率最合适？
q_en: During active coding, what progress narration frequency works best?
options: 每敲几个字符就要播报一次，几乎是逐键播报
大约每 30 到 60 秒说一句进度和原因
只在写完全部代码之后才总结一次进度的情况
完全不说话，靠面试官自己盯着代码来做判断
why: 30-60 秒是经验性节奏参考、不是公式算出来的；太密会打断打字流，太疏又会显得失联。
why_en: Roughly one narration every thirty to sixty seconds is a practical guideline, not a formula, that keeps the interviewer aligned without interrupting your flow.
options_en: Announce progress after nearly every keystroke you type, almost narrating each one.
Say what you're doing and why roughly every 30 to 60 seconds.
Only summarize progress once, after all the code has already been written.
Say nothing at all and let the interviewer track progress from the code by themselves.
optionExplanations: 按键级播报的信息密度太低，面试官会被打字噪音淹没，抓不到重点。
对，30 到 60 秒说一句在做什么、为什么，是不打断打字又不失联的经验节奏。
全部写完才总结，面试官全程只能看操作，判断依据来得太晚。
完全不说话，面试官只能自己盯代码猜，评估窗口基本消失。
optionExplanations_en: Announcing after every few keystrokes buries the signal in typing noise, the interviewer loses the point.
Right — about every 30 to 60 seconds is a practical rhythm that doesn't interrupt flow or go dark.
Summarizing only once everything is written means the interviewer's context arrives far too late.
Saying nothing at all leaves the interviewer guessing from the code alone — the evaluation window is gone.

scenario: 45 分钟面试里你的口头带宽有限，面试官要在结束铃响时给出过程分。
scenario_en: You have limited talking bandwidth in a 45-minute interview, and the interviewer has to score your process the moment time is up.
q: 编码过程中，哪些时刻最值得主动说出来？（多选）
q_en: During coding, which moments are most worth saying out loud? (Select all that apply.)
options: AI 输出和你的预期不一致
每次输入一个标点符号
准备开始实现下一个功能步骤
发现需要改变算法或数据结构
why: 面试官关心决策、偏差和修正，而不是机械的输入细节。
why_en: The interviewer needs decisions, mismatches, and corrections, not keystroke-level commentary.
options_en: The AI's output doesn't match what you expected.
Every time you type a single punctuation mark.
You're about to start the next implementation step.
You realize the algorithm or data structure needs to change.
optionExplanations: 输出跟预期对不上时说出来，能让面试官看到你在核对结果，不是照单全收。
标点级别的播报没有决策信息，纯粹占用本该讲判断的时间。
开始下一步前说一声，面试官提前知道方向，跟得上你的节奏。
算法或结构要变时说清楚，能让面试官看到这是主动调整而非乱改。
optionExplanations_en: Flagging a mismatch between output and expectation shows you're checking results, not accepting them blind.
Punctuation-level narration carries zero decision value, it just eats time you could spend on judgment.
Announcing the next step before you start it keeps the interviewer ahead of your pace.
Naming an algorithm or structure change shows a deliberate adjustment, not a random edit.

scenario: 你需要安静想十几秒，确认当前算法能否覆盖边界情况。
scenario_en: You need to think quietly for ten or so seconds to confirm whether the current algorithm covers edge cases.
q: 这时最合适的处理方式是什么？
q_en: What is the best way to handle this moment?
options: 直接沉默不说话，让面试官自己去猜你在干嘛
还没想清楚就立刻让 AI 生成新方案
说一句“想一下这个边界情况”，再停顿
跳过边界情况不想，直接往下写代码
why: 一句框定语能把沉默变成可理解的思考时间，避免面试官误以为你卡住或走神。
why_en: A short framing sentence turns silence into an understandable thinking pause instead of ambiguous dead air.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经有可运行测试，可以边说边跑测试，用结果帮助思考。
options_en: Go completely silent and let the interviewer guess what you're doing.
Have the AI generate a new approach before you've even thought it through.
Say 'let me think about this edge case' and pause briefly.
Skip the edge case without thinking about it and just keep writing.
tradeoff: 一句框定语再沉默 vs 直接沉默不说明
optionExplanations: 完全沉默，面试官分不清你是在想、卡住了还是走神了。
还没想明白就让 AI 重新生成，容易在没想清楚的情况下越改越乱。
对，一句框定语几乎零成本，就能把沉默变成看得懂的思考停顿。
直接跳过边界情况不想，等于把风险留到后面才爆出来。
optionExplanations_en: Going fully silent leaves the interviewer unable to tell if you're thinking, stuck, or distracted.
Regenerating before you've actually thought it through risks making the mess worse, not better.
Right — one framing sentence costs almost nothing and turns silence into a legible thinking pause.
Skipping the edge case without thinking about it just pushes the risk further down the line.

scenario: 你要让 AI 实现搜索函数，需要让面试官清楚你选的是 BFS，而不是把决策交给 AI。
scenario_en: You want the AI to implement a search function, and the interviewer needs to know you chose BFS rather than handing the decision to the AI.
q: 哪组“口头说明 + 提示”最能体现你在主导决策？
q_en: Which pair of spoken framing and prompt best shows that you are driving the decision?
options: 说明：我先看看 AI 会怎么处理这道题，之后再说。提示：“solve this”
说明：用 BFS 找最短路径。提示：在 Grid 实现 BFS 返回坐标路径。
说明：完全不做任何说明。提示：只写一句“make it work”
说明：AI 应该自己知道要怎么做。提示：“写一个复杂一点的解法”
why: 先公开你的策略，再把同一策略写进提示，能让 AI 输出贴合方案，同时向面试官展示你在做决策。
why_en: State your strategy out loud and put the same strategy in the prompt so the AI executes your decision, not its own.
whenOtherWins: 如果算法选择还没确定，可以先说明你在比较 BFS、DFS 或 Dijkstra，再决定后提示。
options_en: Framing: let's see what the AI does with it first, I'll explain later. Prompt: 'solve this.'
Framing: I'll use BFS for the shortest path. Prompt: implement BFS on Grid, return the coordinate path.
Framing: none at all. Prompt: just 'make it work.'
Framing: the AI should already know what to do. Prompt: 'write a somewhat complex solution.'
tradeoff: 先说策略再写进提示 vs 不说明直接丢给 AI 决定

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按层从起点向外扩展，用于无权图找最短路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, explores a graph layer by layer from the start node and finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索，沿一条路径尽量往前探索，走到底再回溯。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, explores as far as possible along one path before backtracking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理带权图最短路径的经典算法，每次扩展当前已知代价最小的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's Algorithm finds shortest paths in a weighted graph by always expanding the lowest-known-cost node next.

optionExplanations: 只说“看看 AI 怎么处理”再丢一句空提示，算法选择权全交给了 AI。
对，先口头点名 BFS，再把同一约束写进提示，AI 输出直接落在你的方案上。
完全不说明、只给一句“make it work”，AI 可能选出你答不上来的方案。
“AI 应该知道”加一句模糊提示，等于没有给出任何可执行的约束。
optionExplanations_en: Just saying 'let's see what the AI does' plus an empty prompt hands the algorithm choice to the AI entirely.
Right — naming BFS out loud, then encoding the same constraint in the prompt, keeps the AI's output on your plan.
Giving no framing and only 'make it work' risks the AI picking an approach you can't defend.
'The AI should already know' plus a vague prompt gives it nothing executable to build from.

scenario: 面试官当天连排多场，只按现场看到的过程打分，事后不回放你的 AI 对话记录。
scenario_en: The interviewer runs back-to-back sessions and scores only what they see live, with no replay of your AI chat log afterward.
q: 事后解释你刚让 AI 做了什么，为什么弱于提示前先说明？
q_en: Why is explaining what you just asked the AI to do weaker than stating it before prompting?
options: 事后解释会导致 AI 生成的速度变慢
事后解释在大多数面试的规则里是明确被禁止的
两种方式对面试官来说完全没有区别
事前说明让面试官实时看到计划，而不是事后倒推
why: 面试评估的是过程控制；事前说明能让你的意图在行动发生的同时就被看到。
why_en: Interviews evaluate process control, and explaining before you act makes your intent visible in real time.
options_en: Explaining after the fact makes the AI's generation speed slower.
Explaining after the fact is explicitly against the rules in most interviews.
The two approaches make no difference at all to the interviewer.
Explaining beforehand lets the interviewer see your plan in real time, instead of reconstructing it afterward.
optionExplanations: 叙述时机跟 AI 生成速度是两回事，两者之间没有因果关系。
大多数面试其实允许事后解释，只是信号强度更弱，不是被禁止。
时机差异正是这题的关键，先说和后说对面试官的可读性完全不同。
对，事前说明能让面试官在动作发生的同时就看到你的计划，不用事后靠猜。
optionExplanations_en: Narration timing and AI generation speed are unrelated, there's no causal link there.
Most interviews actually allow after-the-fact explanation, it's just a weaker signal, not a rule violation.
The timing gap is exactly the point here — before and after read very differently to the interviewer.
Right — explaining beforehand lets the interviewer watch your plan unfold live instead of reconstructing it later.

scenario: AI 一次性输出了一大段代码，你还没有读完确认。
scenario_en: The AI produced a large block of code all at once, and you have not finished reviewing it.
q: 这时最好的口头反馈是什么？
q_en: What is the best spoken response here?
options: “看起来应该可以，我们继续下一步吧。”
“我不需要看这段代码，直接拿去用。”
“这段挺长，我先读一遍确认它符合计划。”
“面试官你能不能帮我读一下这段？”
why: 承认需要审阅是好信号，说明你不会因为代码看起来完整就直接接受。
why_en: Saying you need to review a large output shows you won't accept complete-looking code blindly.
whenOtherWins: 如果输出只是一行你能立刻确认的改动，可以快速说明确认点后继续。
options_en: 'Looks fine, let's go ahead and move on to the next step.'
'I don't need to look at this code, I'll just use it.'
'This is a lot, let me read through it to confirm it matches the plan.'
'Can you go read through this section for me instead?'
tradeoff: 承认需要审阅 vs 假设输出直接可信
optionExplanations: “应该可以”是没核实过的猜测，面试官会当成你在盲目接受输出。
完全不看直接用，风险等到后面测试或追问时才会暴露出来。
对，主动说要先读一遍再判断，把审阅习惯摆在明面上给面试官看。
把审阅甩给面试官，本该是候选人自己的职责，显得缺乏主导。
optionExplanations_en: 'Should be fine' is an unverified guess, it reads as accepting the output blindly.
Skipping the read entirely just delays the risk until testing or a follow-up question exposes it.
Right — saying you'll read it first before continuing puts your review habit on full display.
Handing review to the interviewer is your job to begin with, it makes you look less in control.

q: 补全沟通节奏的练习方法：
q_en: Complete the practice method for building communication rhythm:
text: 用 AI 解题时录下自己，回看哪里{{沉默太久}}、哪里{{过度叙述}}，几次练习后会形成自然节奏。
why: 沟通节奏很难只靠阅读形成，录像回放能立刻暴露盲点。
why_en: Recording practice sessions exposes long silences and over-narration so you can tune your rhythm.

scenario: 面试只剩 20 分钟还有两个函数要写，你说的每句话都在花掉这个时间预算。
scenario_en: There are 20 minutes left and two functions still to write, so every sentence you say spends part of that budget.
q: 编码过程中，哪句话属于过度叙述而非有用沟通？
q_en: During coding, which sentence is over-narration rather than useful communication?
options: “我现在要输入 function 这个单词。”
“我接下来实现 search 函数。”
“这段输出用了错误的错误处理风格，我会重提示。”
“我需要想一下这个边界情况。”
why: 有用沟通聚焦决策和状态，机械播报键盘动作只会消耗时间和注意力。
why_en: Useful narration covers decisions and state, while keystroke-level commentary just wastes time and attention.
options_en: 'I'm about to type the word function now.'
'I'm going to implement the search function next.'
'This output uses the wrong error-handling style, I'll reprompt it.'
'I need to think about this edge case for a second.'
tradeoff: 播报决策和状态 vs 播报键盘动作
optionExplanations: 对，播报到具体单词级别没有任何判断信息，纯粹是键盘动作的噪音。
宣布下一步要实现什么，是决策级信息，值得说，不算过度叙述。
指出风格冲突并打算重提示，是主动纠偏的证据，同样值得说。
提前说一句要想边界情况，把停顿变得可理解，也不算过度。
optionExplanations_en: Right — narrating down to a single word carries zero judgment, it's pure keystroke noise.
Announcing the next thing you'll implement is decision-level information, worth saying, not over-narration.
Flagging a style conflict and planning to reprompt is proof of self-correction, also worth saying.
A quick heads-up before thinking through an edge case makes the pause legible, not excessive.

scenario: 面试第 35 分钟测试突然全红，面试官要在剩下 25 分钟里判断你的调试能力。
scenario_en: At minute 35 the whole test suite goes red, and the interviewer has 25 minutes left to judge how you debug.
q: 出问题时，哪些沟通动作能把局面拉回可评估状态？（多选）
q_en: When something goes wrong, which communication moves bring the situation back into an evaluable state? (Select all that apply.)
options: 说明当前错误或阻塞点
给出你对根因的判断
解释为什么要改变方向
静默删除大量代码，不作说明
why: 问题本身不可怕，可怕的是面试官看不到你如何诊断和调整。
why_en: When things go wrong, visible diagnosis and explicit adjustment matter more than hiding the struggle.
options_en: Name the current error or blocker.
State your judgment about the root cause.
Explain why you're changing direction.
Silently delete a large chunk of code without explanation.
optionExplanations: 把卡点具体说出来，是让面试官重新跟上进度的第一步。
给出根因判断，把“出问题了”升级成“我知道为什么”，可评估。
解释转向的理由，能把主动调整和随意乱改区分开来。
静默删除一大块代码不说明，面试官只看到混乱，判断不出你的依据。
optionExplanations_en: Naming the blocker concretely is the first step to getting the interviewer back up to speed.
Stating your root-cause judgment upgrades 'something's wrong' into something evaluable.
Explaining the reason for a pivot separates a deliberate adjustment from a random rewrite.
Silently deleting a big chunk of code with no explanation just looks like chaos to the interviewer.

scenario: 面试官已经看过很多候选人做同一道题，熟悉常见的死路在哪里。
scenario_en: The interviewer has seen many candidates solve this same problem and knows the common dead ends.
q: 你走进死路时，最应该向面试官展示什么？
q_en: When you hit a dead end, what should you most show the interviewer?
options: 永远不承认自己走错方向
继续微调错误方向直到时间用完
把责任推给 AI 的建议
尽快识别死路、说明原因并干净转向
why: 面试官不指望你避开所有死路，但会评估你发现和恢复的速度。
why_en: Interviewers don't expect you to avoid every dead end, but they do evaluate how fast you notice and recover.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是实现细节的小错，先局部修正即可；只有方向性错误才需要明确转向。
options_en: Never admit you went the wrong way.
Keep tweaking the wrong direction until time runs out.
Blame the AI's suggestion for the wrong turn.
Recognize the dead end quickly, explain why, and pivot cleanly.
tradeoff: 快速识别并转向 vs 硬撑原方向到超时
optionExplanations: 死不承认走错方向，面试官很快就能看穿，可信度反而更受损。
在错误方向上死磕到超时，是时间耗尽还没有可用方案的最差结果。
把方向判断甩给 AI 建议，决策权始终在你手里，这个借口站不住。
对，尽快认出死路、讲清原因、干净转向，正是面试官在评估的恢复速度。
optionExplanations_en: Refusing to admit a wrong turn gets seen through fast, and it costs you credibility instead of saving it.
Grinding on a broken direction until time's up is one of the worst outcomes: no usable solution left.
Blaming the AI's suggestion doesn't hold up, the decision was always yours to make.
Right — recognizing the dead end fast, explaining why, and pivoting cleanly is exactly what gets evaluated.

q: 把“AI 输出不符合项目风格”后的沟通链排好：
q_en: Put the communication chain in order after the AI output does not match the project style:
steps: 重新提示 AI 使用项目现有错误处理风格
说明你观察到它用了异常而项目用 error object
继续前先读生成的改动是否符合预期
指出这会和代码库模式冲突
why: 先说观察，再说影响，然后重定向 AI，最后审阅结果，能完整展示控制力。
why_en: The correction loop is observe, explain impact, reprompt with constraints, then review the revised output.
tradeoff: 观察+影响+重定向+复核的完整闭环 vs 直接静默重写
diagram:
flowchart LR
  BadStyle[Output off style] --> Say[Name mismatch]
  Say --> Reprompt[Reprompt with local pattern]
  Reprompt --> Review[Review diff]
  Review --> Test[Run tests]
  Test --> Explain[Explain outcome]
